summary: "This ALWAYS happens in an Oil Crisis - Buy THIS Instead!" (Business With Brian, 2026-03-24) uses 50 years of historical data to argue against the consensus trade during the Strait of Hormuz oil crisis (oil hit $119 intraday, ~200 tankers anchored, CNBC calling it the biggest supply disruption in history at 3x the 1973 embargo). Central claim: five oil spikes in 50 years (1973, 1979, 1990, 2008, 2022) all reversed, and the reactionary trade — buy energy, sell tech — was wrong long-term all five times. He concedes this crisis is scarier than most (a physical disruption closest to 1979, SPR at just 58% of capacity at 415M barrels, OPEC's 5M bpd spare capacity stranded behind Hormuz) but argues the math is different today: oil is only 0.4% of US GDP versus 1.5% in 1979, so the economy is 70% less oil-dependent. The 2022 playbook is his template: oil spiked to $130, the Nasdaq fell 33%, then oil was back under $100 within four months — buying QQQ at the bottom delivered an 87% trough-to-peak swing. Geopolitical statistics: the average S&P 500 drawdown in major shocks is -4.7%, bottoming in ~19 days and recovering in ~42, with the index higher 12 months later 70% of the time — what matters is whether a recession follows, which an oil-driven downturn is less likely to cause now.
